identity.title: Deletion of the immune evasion gene gG enhances cellular immunity and protective efficacy of the quadruple-deleted feline herpesvirus type 1 recombinant FHV-DeltaTK/gI/gE/gG.

content.abstract: Feline herpesvirus type 1 (FHV-1) causes feline viral rhinotracheitis (FVR), which can cause severe disease in kittens. Our previously developed recombinant virus, FHV-DeltaTK/gI/gE, provided enhanced protection compared with existing vaccines; however, its protective efficacy requires further improvement. Therefore, optimization of this vaccine by deleting additional nonvirulence genes involved in immune evasion is warranted. Glycoprotein G (gG) of alphaherpesviruses has been implicated in immune evasion, but its role in FHV-1 immune modulation and vaccine efficacy remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that gG overexpression significantly downregulated the expression of chemokines, including CCL and CXCL family members, interferon-beta (IFN-beta), and interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs), whereas gG deletion partially alleviated this suppression. Subsequently, a recombinant virus designated FHV-DeltaTK/gI/gE/gG was generated by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of the gG gene from the FHV-DeltaTK/gI/gE backbone. The resulting recombinant virus exhibited growth kinetics comparable to those of FHV-DeltaTK/gI/gE in vitro. FHV-DeltaTK/gI/gE/gG was safe in kittens, and subcutaneous prime-boost immunization provided enhanced protection against the virulent FHV-1 WH2020 strain. Compared with control kittens, those vaccinated with FHV-DeltaTK/gI/gE/gG exhibited milder clinical signs, lower viral loads in tissues, significantly elevated serum IFN-gamma levels, and significantly upregulated expression of chemokines and innate immune factors in the nasal turbinates following challenge. Collectively, these findings suggest that FHV-1 gG contributes to the suppression of host innate immune responses and its deletion from DeltaTK/gI/gE backbone enhances cellular immunity, thereby improving protection against challenge and reducing wild-type viral colonization in tissues. FHV-DeltaTK/gI/gE/gG represents a promising live attenuated vaccine candidate against FHV-1.
